A visible stack with counted instances (say 1 live, within 64) plus 1024 switched-off instances has 1025 mapped and is refused whole with effects_over_budget: a rendered stack is lost because of the count of its switched-off instances, which is the R10 FAIL shape (a bound on unrendered instances costing rendered effects) at the per-stack level, and the lane's own V4-06 class text names 'a cap (per layer or per document, counted or uncounted) whose crossing refuses or drops a stack of the OTHER category'. new_findings.evidence: Two layer classes are counted by the importer but never counted by a plan: layers with no pixels and clipped layers whose base is hidden or empty. Because a counted stack past 4096 is lost whole (effects.rs:153-155), such layers can make the importer refuse a later layer that a plan would render (visible live stack lost with effects_over_document_budget while the plan's own count is <= 4096). It needs > 4096 apparent counted instances, so it is unreachable for ordinary documents, but it is the same 'unrendered content decides the fate of rendered content' pattern as R9/R10, and it is disclosed only in the kernel lane file: the shipped rule text (effects.rs:35-47, proposal.rs:501-504, DESCRIPTOR clause 1) says the count is the plan's. Every test fixture is a no-pixel layer (effects_budget.rs:189-200), so the tests assert the importer's rule, not the plan's.
